notes: Intro: Helix builds an IDE copilot (VSCode + JetBrains) focused on low-latency inline completions and multi-line suggestions.
Primary ask: TTFT (time-to-first-token) and stable typing experience — target median TTFT <= 75ms, p95 < 200ms. Users report visible jitter > 250ms is unacceptable.
Token budget model: prefer token-budget-per-keystroke + short completion budget fallback. Want control over per-session vs per-completion budgets to avoid runaway cost during long refactors.

Streaming behavior: need continuous streaming with partial token flushes for first N tokens to reduce perceived latency (prefetch + early flush). Backpressure: VSCode extension must be able to pause/resume stream when local editor buffer is saturated.

Model/version preferences: want ability to pin to a quantized 13B variant for most completions, with automatic fallback to a higher-quality 33B only for multi-line refactors. Version pin per route + rollout windows.
Cost sensitivity: mid-market ARR cap; looking to optimize batching and prefix caching across users in org to reduce token spend by ~20-40%.
Security: SSO + SCIM mandatory, audit logs required for all inference requests; EU customers require data residency and optional KMS key ownership.

POC plan accepted: 2-week VSCode extension POC, 10 internal devs, compare three configs: 1) streaming low-latency (small model, aggressive early flush), 2) batched higher-throughput (larger model, caching), 3) hybrid with model routing based on request complexity.
POC success metrics: TTFT median + p95; completion coherence score (dev eval set); cost per 1000 completions; perceived jitter (dev survey).
Recent activity: 2026-02-10 kickoff call (ff-20260210-gj3k) — collected initial TTFT traces from alpha extension (attached). 2026-02-24 architecture deep-dive with Diego + infra (ff-20260224-xb9p).
Quote from head of eng: "If we can get first-token under 100ms for single-line completions, adoption jump will be immediate."

Integration notes: extension uses websocket streaming; needs Redwood SDK support for explicit backpressure control and per-char early-flush thresholds. Current blocker: no polished SDK hook for pausing token stream mid-response.
Legal/Procurement: vendor risk questionnaire started; data residency clause requested for EU customers; procurement expects SOW with SLA on TTFT jitter and incident response times.
Engineering asks for Redwood: SDK hook to set token_budget_mode, early_flush_tokens, pause_on_buffer_full flag, and telemetry endpoint for per-keystroke latency traces.
Logged leads: potential Dedicated reserved pool for orgs > 200 devs; initial proposal includes a small Dedicated cluster for Europe and hosted fallback in NA.
